newsitem.title: BELARUS: U.S. protests Belarus barring of top aide official.
newsitem.headline: U.S. protests Belarus barring of top aide official.

text.p: The United States embassy protested to Belarus on Monday after the local executive director of the Soros Foundation was barred from the former Soviet republic.
State-run television said earlier on Monday that U.S. citizen Peter Bern was accused of supporting the opposition and was barred from re-entering the country for interfering in Belarussian affairs.

The foundation, set up by Hungarian-born American billionaire George Soros, has invested $13 million in Belarus, including $6 million last year mostly for education, ecological and medical programmes.

The television presenter added that Bern was accused of taking part in mass actions organised by the opposition and aired pictures, provided by the KGB security service, showing him watching a recent opposition rally from the sidelines.
"The barring of the opposition's best friend will not mean any difficulties for the Soros Foundation's activities in Belarus," the TV presenter said.
"But lists of those who have been given grants from this foundation will be published soon and people will know who they are," he added.
Bern, who was based in Minsk, arrived on Sunday afternoon from a meeting in Budapest, but was then put on a plane to Frankfurt.

"We intended to meet Bern at the airport but were barred from doing so. They didn't even allow us to talk to him," said Roman Yakovlevsky, a Belarussian member of the foundation's management in Minsk.

U.S. Ambassador to Belarus Kenneth Yalovitz cancelled a visit to Grodno on the Polish border where he intended to take part in the ceremony marking the opening of housing for servicemen built with American financial help.

"The American Embassy in Belarus has made an official protest to the Belarussian Foreign Ministry concerning the barring of entrance of a U.S. citizen to the country," spokeswoman Alexei Solomakha said. "Belarus violated international norms."
She added that Yalovitz expressed dissatisfaction with the incident in talks with Foreign Ministry officials.
